title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio discusses U.S.-Japan alliance with Foreign Minister Motegi
excerpt: The officials coordinated ahead of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta following a discussion on security and recent events in Okinawa.
bodyHtml:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu on October 10, 2026. The two officials reaffirmed the U.S.-Japan Alliance, which the U.S. State Department described as the cornerstone of peace, security, and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond.

During the call, Secretary Rubio expressed condolences regarding the death of a Japanese national in Okinawa. He stated that the United States is determined to communicate and cooperate with the Government of Japan and local authorities during their investigation.

Secretary Rubio also raised the necessity of U.S. sanctions on the International Criminal Court, citing what he described as the Court’s rogue actions that threaten American sovereignty. The Secretary and Foreign Minister Motegi committed to continued close coordination ahead of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta.
